summary.title: Life Is Not Short
summary.one_liner: Seneca's views on why life feels short (we waste time, defer living, and chase empty goals) and how to spend it well by studying philosophy and living intentionally.
keywords: philosophy as a way to extend life
takeaways: Seneca argues life is long enough; people waste it on distractions and trivia rather than lacking time.
Deferring life ('when I retire I'll live') is the biggest waste, since the future is uncertain and the present is what you control.
Spend time intentionally and avoid people and things that do not matter, treating time as more valuable than property.
Studying philosophers from the past is presented as a way to absorb their experience and effectively extend your life.
Each footnote gives a direct quote from Seneca's essay 'On the Shortness of Life', so the page doubles as a readable excerpt of the original.
summary.summary: This is a fictional interview format blog post in which the author has Seneca answer questions about the shortness of life, based on his essay 'On the Shortness of Life'. Seneca's answers are presented as direct quotes or paraphrases, and numbered footnotes give the original Latin-derived source text for each response. Topics include wasting time, the folly of deferred life plans, the emptiness of chasing power and pleasure, and the value of reading philosophy. The page ends with a short promotional note about the blog, which is kept out of this summary.
